intro_html: Fried rice built on ground beef, which is cheaper than takeout and loaded with more protein. Each bowl carries 46 grams for about $4.94 (at everyday cost), and the pan makes 14 servings. This is the perfect home for leftover rice, and it beats the delivery version every time.
cost_closing_html: About $4.94 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 bowls serves 46 grams of protein at 593 calories, turning a takeout treat into a meal-prep workhorse.
upsell_html: The cure for leftover rice and takeout cravings in one skillet. Cook once, eat all week. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Use day-old cold rice if you can. It fries up firmer and cheaper than any restaurant version and keeps this recipe from going gummy.
A bag of frozen peas and carrots costs next to nothing, never spoils, and cooks straight from the freezer.
Soy sauce and sesame oil are the only special buys, and both last months, so you are set for many batches to come.
make_it: Brown 5.4 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain.
Toss in the peas and carrots and cook until they warm through.
Add the cooked rice, ideally day-old and cold, so it fries up instead of turning mushy.
Drizzle in the soy sauce and sesame oil with the garlic and ginger, stirring until everything is coated.
Push it around the hot skillet a couple minutes to get that fried-rice edge, then portion out.
